workflows.title: One School Dossier
workflows.audience: journalists, researchers, families, and campus groups
steps: Open the school dossier and read the use-limit block before interpreting counts.
Inspect the timeline, response records, legal or OCR items, and related sources.
Export a Research Workspace packet for the records you intend to cite.
supported_claims: The archive contains public-source records for this school in the current snapshot.
requires_followup: Claims about safety, frequency, intent, liability, or campus climate require primary-source and institutional follow-up.

workflows.title: One Public Record
steps: Find the record in Events and open the event detail page.
Read the Record Audit card, source list, confidence label, and correction path.
Open the source page and external source before reusing the record.
supported_claims: A specific public-source record exists and is linked to a current snapshot hash.
requires_followup: Disputed facts, legal conclusions, and institutional intent require source reading and direct follow-up.

workflows.title: Legal or OCR Trail
steps: Filter Events for OCR, lawsuit, Title VI, Title IX, settlement, resolution, or complaint terms.
Open each event and compare legal-status wording against linked public sources.
Export a packet and request comment before making claims beyond the public record.
supported_claims: The archive identifies public legal or OCR-related documentation currently linked to records.
requires_followup: Procedural posture, liability, findings, settlement meaning, and current status require primary-source legal review.

workflows.title: Institutional Response Trail
steps: Search Events or a school dossier for response records.
Compare response dates and wording against linked source material.
Export only the response records needed for the narrow question.
supported_claims: The archive documents public institutional-response language linked to specific records.
requires_followup: Effectiveness, sincerity, completeness, and implementation require additional reporting.

workflows.title: Source Audit Follow-Up
steps: Open the Reviewer Queue and locate source-audit follow-up samples.
Open each source page and external source URL.
Report dead links, redirects, publisher changes, or better stable sources through the correction workflow.
supported_claims: The archive exposes source URLs that may need maintenance or replacement.
requires_followup: A failed automated URL check does not prove the source is unavailable; manual review is required.

workflows.title: Methodology Review Sample
steps: Choose a fixed review sample from the Reviewer Queue.
Check each record against the codebook, source text, and Record Audit card.
Document findings through the reviewer checklist without treating review as approval.
supported_claims: A bounded sample can be reviewed for source support, classification, and use-limit quality.
requires_followup: A sample review does not validate the full archive or imply organizational support.

workflows.title: Narrow Research Packet
steps: Write a narrow question before selecting records.
Search and select only records needed for that question.
Export markdown or JSON with snapshot hash and use limits.
supported_claims: Selected public-source records can support a narrow documentation question.
requires_followup: Patterns in a selected packet cannot be generalized into frequency claims or school comparisons.

workflows.title: Correction or Duplicate Report
steps: Identify the record ID and the field or duplicate relationship to review.
Find a public source URL supporting the correction or duplicate report.
Generate a structured packet and submit it through the matching issue template.
supported_claims: A source-backed correction or duplicate report can be prepared for review.
requires_followup: A submitted packet does not change the public dataset until review is complete.
